title: Multi-tenant fallback contours and preemption safeguard PRD
creator: Priya Raman
overview: Problem: Customers using Dedicated capacity experience intermittent latency spikes and failed requests during cross-tenant hotspots and cloud preemption events. Current fallback behavior is binary (fully allow or fully reject) and lacks predictable QoS guarantees. This PRD defines a multi-tier fallback contour and preemption safeguard that protects reserved-pool SLAs while providing predictable, graceful degradation for lower-priority tenants and burst users.
background: Redwood Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools to tenants with SLA commitments. During surge windows or underlying infra pressure (zonal preemption, node reclamation, noisy neighbors), we either throttle aggressively or route to opportunistic pools which often violates latency SLOs. Engineering has prototypes for soft-evict hooks and headroom buckets; PM has prioritized predictable tenant behavior for renewals and enterprise contracts.
goals: 1) Ensure reserved-tier requests meet latency and availability targets during common degradation modes (zonal preemption, transient hotspot). 2) Provide transparent, documented fallback contours for how traffic is degraded across priority classes. 3) Implement preemption-safe admission controls and a grace-based eviction policy to avoid cascading failures. 4) Give Console visibility (per-tenant) into active fallback state and projected impact. 5) Keep changes compatible with Dedicated autoscaling and existing burst windows.
non_goals: 1) Replacing long-term capacity planning tools. 2) Building a fully decentralized smart router (this is a centralized policy layer). 3) Changing per-token pricing or contract terms in this rollout.
key_user_stories: - As a platform reliability owner, I need deterministic behavior when nodes are reclaimed so I can promise SLA containment to reserved tenants. - As a tenant admin, I need visibility into fallback state and a way to opt into controlled degradation (e.g., reduced max tokens) instead of hard outage. - As an on-call engineer, I need playbook steps and automated signals to quickly restore normal routing after a transient hotspot.
requirements:
Functional requirements:
1) Fallback contours: define at least three fallback contours (Green: full service, Amber: soft-degrade, Red: emergency throttle). Each contour maps to admission controls, max-concurrent-requests, and allowed burst window sizes.
2) Priority-aware admission controller: evaluate incoming requests with tenant priority, reservation status, and historical headroom credit to accept, queue briefly, or reject with a clear rejection reason.
3) Preemption-safe soft-eviction: allow in-flight low-priority requests to finish up to a short grace window (configurable 3-10s) before evicting KV cache or reclaiming GPU.
4) Headroom credits ledger: a per-tenant decaying credit that allows controlled bursts across short windows; credits accrue with idle capacity and are debited on burst.
5) Console and API exposure: status endpoint and Console widget showing active contour, projected latency impact, and remaining headroom credits.
6) Metrics & alerts: per-tenant SLO compliance, per-contour request acceptance rate, tail latency P95/P99, preemption events count, and headroom exhaustion rate.
7) Config knobs: contour thresholds, grace window, credit accrual rate, emergency fallback percent, and per-tenant exemption flags for platinum contracts.

Non-functional requirements:
1) The admission controller must add <2ms median overhead to request path in steady-state.
2) Changes must be backward compatible with existing Dedicated routing and autoscaler.
3) Feature flags for gradual rollout: canary tenants, staged regional enablement, and per-customer opt-in/opt-out.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Unit/integration tests cover admission logic across all contours and show expected accept/reject decisions for synthetic traffic patterns. 2) In canary region (us-west-2) with 3 pilot tenants, system demonstrates: reserved-tier P95 latency degradation <10% during artificially injected 20% node loss and no more than 2 visible failed requests per minute attributable to our controller. 3) Headroom ledger correctly accrues and debits credits in 1-minute resolution and shows correct values in Console for pilot tenants. 4) Console displays contour state and associated mitigation actions. 5) Operational runbook documented with playbook steps and automation to rollback to previous routing. 6) No >5% increase in median latency for green-contour requests in steady-state post-deploy. 7) Security review completed if security_review_required is true.
metrics_and_success: Primary metrics: reserved-tier P95 and P99 latency, reserved-tier availability (errors per 1M requests), headroom exhaustion rate, number of preemption-triggered evictions, and successful graceful evictions vs abrupt kills. Success targets for GA: reserved-tier P95 degradation <=10% during 20% capacity loss scenarios; availability >= 99.95% in non-emergency windows; clear Console visibility for all pilot tenants.
implementation_notes:
- Admission controller will be implemented as a lightweight policy layer colocated with the routing tier; evaluate language/runtime consistent with runtime team recommendations.
- Use existing KV cache eviction hooks where possible; add a 'soft-evict' state that delays destructive evictions for the configured grace window.
- Headroom ledger implemented in the telemetry service with a 1-minute rollup; ensure write path is resilient and eventual-consistent.
- Add feature flags and per-tenant config stored in the Dedicated config service; ensure atomic read on request admission.
- Coordinate with Dedicated autoscaler team to avoid conflicting prewarm decisions; define a small sync API between controller and autoscaler.
- Create a synthetic test harness to simulate zonal preemption and noisy-neighbor loads for automated canary tests.
rollout_plan:
1) Experimental: enable for internal tenants only (2 weeks) and run chaos tests. 2) Canary: enable in us-west-2 for 3 pilot tenants for 2 weeks, monitor metrics & exec on-call runbook. 3) Gradual: expand to <10% of Dedicated capacity over 4 weeks, monitor and tweak knobs. 4) GA: full enable with defaults and documented opt-out for enterprise customers.
Rollback criteria: sustained >10% increase in reserved-tier P95 for >30 minutes or >0.1% new user-facing errors traced to admission controller after mitigation steps fail.
open_questions: 1) What exact credit accrual model (linear, exponential decay) minimizes gaming while being intuitive for customers? 2) Where should per-tenant exemption flags live and who can modify them? 3) What default contour thresholds balance safety and customer experience? 4) Should the headroom ledger be strongly consistent or eventual-consistent given performance tradeoffs?
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Admission controller bugs could incorrectly reject high-priority traffic. Mitigation: extensive unit tests, staged canary, and emergency bypass flag.
Risk: Headroom ledger performance causing request path latency. Mitigation: implement ledger reads cached locally with 1s TTL and periodic refresh.
Risk: Complex knobs confuse customers. Mitigation: provide Console presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and clear docs.
Risk: Interactions with autoscaler cause oscillation. Mitigation: coordinate API and rate-limit inter-component signals; add hysteresis in decisions.
